EKZA
Create once. Own it. Play it across games.

Ekza combines AI-assisted 3D creation, a persistent player profile and partner integrations so one owned avatar can have approved, game-ready versions across multiple titles.

02Problem

AI can generate an asset.
It still cannot make it playable everywhere.

Image and 3D models make creation faster, but raw output is rarely rigged, optimized, licensed or compatible with a real game. Player identity also remains locked inside separate game accounts.

Generation gap

Prompts produce concepts or base meshes, not production-ready characters.

Closed identity

Players rebuild their avatar and repurchase similar items in every game.

Integration cost

Studios repeat rigging, optimization, engine setup and QA for each title.

03Interoperability

Cross-game does not mean
one file fits every game.

Art direction, skeletons, animation systems, polygon budgets, materials and gameplay rules differ. A portable asset needs a shared identity plus an approved rendition for every partner game.

04Solution

One player profile connects
every approved game version.

An asset passport links source, ownership, permissions and revenue rules to game-specific renditions - including Cocos Creator for Weixin and Tuanjie for Douyin.

“One owned identity. Multiple game-ready renditions.” The Ekza asset passport

06User profile

The user profile is the portable layer.

Players see what they own, which games support it and which approved rendition will load. Partner games read a simple entitlement and retrieve the correct asset version.

Player sees

Owned assets, compatible games, active avatar and creation history.

Partner reads

Entitlement, approved rendition, license and current asset version.

No wallet-first UX. Players use normal accounts and payments; rights and revenue can settle through conventional contracts, with Solana as an optional verification rail.
Normal account UX · conventional settlement · optional verification rail06 / 15
07Product

Four product layers make AI assets
usable across games.

Ekza unifies user creation, persistent identity, asset records and game delivery. The model provider and blockchain can change without breaking the user relationship.

The moat compounds with each partner: requirements schema, rendition history, entitlement adapters and reusable QA baselines - not one foundation model.

09First commercial pilot

One avatar collection.
Two partner games.

A focused pilot co-creates a small collection, produces a master plus title-specific versions, and connects them through one player profile.

  • Shared creative brief - one recognizable character collection.
  • Concrete deliverables - one master, two approved renditions and two partner integrations.
  • Success criterion - entitlement and partner QA pass in both games.
target: 8-12 weeks after discovery → one collection → two live games
Omoba supplies the controlled reference; Beijing supplies partner distribution09 / 15
